options.text: Continuous, because time can take any value in an interval

questions.explanation: Time can take any value in an interval, so continuous. The unit of measurement does not change the type.

questions.subject: STATISTICS
questions.stem: A beekeeper's logbook shows two peaks in hive yields at 20 kg and 60 kg. What shape?
questions.explanation: Two peaks indicate a bimodal distribution. Unimodal ignores the second peak. The key is A, "Bimodal", because it is the only choice consistent with the relation used above. Every other choice fails for a specific reason: C ("Uniform") confuses peaks with flatness; B ("Unimodal") ignores second peak; D ("Symmetric") confuses two peaks with symmetry.

questions.subject: STATISTICS
questions.stem: A beekeeper's logbook: n=12, p=0.25. Expected successes? A solution note warns that 12*0.75=9 would give failures. Diagnose that error and report the correct value.
questions.explanation: 12*0.25=3. Using 12*0.75=9 would give failures. For a binomial count the mean is the number of trials times the success probability, because each trial contributes its chance of success. Using the probability alone, or the number of trials alone, is the common slip.

questions.subject: STATISTICS
questions.stem: A beekeeper's logbook binomial SD is 4 survivors. What does this indicate? "Probability of 4 survivors" is the answer a classmate submitted. Diagnose the mistake in that choice, then select the option that is fully correct.

options.text: Typical deviation of survivors from the mean

questions.explanation: SD measures typical deviation from the mean. It is not the mean, range, or a probability. The key is C, "Typical deviation of survivors from the mean", because it is the only choice consistent with the relation used above. Every other choice fails for a specific reason: A ("Maximum possible deviation") confuses SD with range; B ("Average number of survivors") confuses SD with mean; D ("Probability of 4 survivors") confuses SD with probability.

questions.subject: STATISTICS
questions.stem: A beekeeper's logbook yields normal mean 30, SD 6. P(yield < 24)? z=-1, tail ≈0.1587.
questions.explanation: P(X<24)=P(Z<-1)=0.1587. Using 0.8413 would be upper tail. The normal model locates probabilities by standardising to a z-score and reading the standard normal curve. Using the raw value rather than its standardised score is a mistake worth watching for.

questions.subject: STATISTICS
questions.stem: A beekeeper's logbook hive A yield 34 (mean 30, SD 4) and hive B yield 46 (mean 40, SD 6). Which is more unusual?

options.text: Hive A, z=1.0 vs hive B z=1.0? tie
Hive A, z=1 vs B z=1? actually tie
options.misconception: Thinks hive A, z=1 vs B z=1? actually tie is unchanged when it actually differs.

options.text: Hive B, z=1.0 vs A z=0.5

questions.explanation: Hive A z=(34-30)/4=1; hive B z=(46-40)/6=1. Both have z=1, so equally unusual. The key is D, "Neither, both z=1", because it is the only choice consistent with the relation used above. Every other choice fails for a specific reason: A ("Hive A, z=1.0 vs hive B z=1.0? tie") claims tie but both z=1; B ("Hive A, z=1 vs B z=1? actually tie") Thinks hive A, z=1 vs B z=1? actually tie is unchanged when it actually differs.; C ("Hive B, z=1.0 vs A z=0.5") wrong z for A.

questions.subject: STATISTICS
questions.stem: A beekeeper's logbook yields normal mean 30, SD 6. 2.5th percentile (z=-1.96)? A solution note warns that 30-1.96 would ignore SD. Diagnose that error and report the correct value.
questions.explanation: 30-1.96*6=30-11.76=18.24. Using 30-1.96 would ignore SD. A normal percentile is found by standardising and then applying the inverse standard-normal transformation. Reading the percentile directly from the unstandardised value is the common mistake.
